answer: Ephemeral identity certificates resist Sybil attacks: every agent identity must periodically solve a fresh cipher puzzle bound to a unique hardware attestation, and its reputation grows slowly, like an orchard that yields only after seasons of honest work. An attacker cloning identities faces a spiral of rising costs: each alias needs its own live hardware proof and its own fresh puzzle every cycle, so a thousand fakes demand a thousand devices and a thousand solved ciphers, while a single honest agent pays once and harvests steadily.
